A format check on an optional create or PATCH field refuses (400); it is never the field's `present` gate. As a `present` gate it skipped the value, and the write succeeded without it: a Jira key or a Linear identifier in `parentId` vanished. Check presence first, then the writable contract, then the format (`routes/proxy-writes.js`, LIN-4451 create, LIN-4452 PATCH).

A typed error a provider method gains reaches a caller only if every route calling that method maps it: `refs`/`partial` in the proxy write `SPEC`, and each session or feedback catch by hand. Provider tests passed while all three create lanes answered a bare 500 for a landed create. Pin it at the route boundary (`routes/proxy-writes.js`; `tests/unit/lin-4452-create-lane-envelope.test.js`).

Every proxy write mount names its operation: `requireWriteScope('<op>')` for a readWrite route, `requireStageWrite('<op>')` for a grant-gated one, with `<op>` in `STAGE_WRITE_OPS` (`lib/stage-writes.js`; the gate is `lib/stage-write-gate.js`). A stamped token is refused any operation its allowance does not list, so a route nobody named would be refused to a reading stage without a word, and an unnamed name throws at mount. A new write route adds its operation to that list and a row to `CENSUS` in `tests/unit/lin-4468-stage-write-allowance.test.js`, or the census fails (LIN-4468).

A token minted for a stage carries its `writes` and ticket, or has a reason not to. Pass both into the mint helpers (`lib/proxy-preamble.js`), or read them from the row (`lib/item-stage-stamp.js`). A wake, immediate or held, takes the stamp of the session it resumes, the parent, not the row that reported (`stampForWakeParent`; a held release gets the producing build's id from the store). A mint with neither is unrestricted, which is right only for a person's or a `custom` mint, listed with its reason in `tests/unit/dispatch-entrance-mint-sweep.test.js`. The refire broker minted unrestricted tokens for read-only rows because its mint was a bare `createToken`, which no helper-name search finds (LIN-4468).

A page script's second request keeps the poll's discipline: coalesce every reason into one fetch per window, and stop when the poll stops (hidden tab, 401, revoked link). `createTimelineRefresher` (`public/task-page.js`, LIN-4405) is the pattern; a running chip changes the poll's track about once a minute, so "fetch when it changes" alone repeats. Done reads once more first (`finish`): the poll that says done carries the last change, and stopping drops it.

The no-build-step rule (`CLAUDE.md`) allows browser sharing, not only forbids it (LIN-4446). The browser may import natively, and the restated copies came from reading the rule as "no sharing" (`docs/papers/harbour/the-second-copy.md` §9–10). Pages become ES modules that import what they share (LIN-4471), converted top down: a page module before the files it uses. A module runs after every classic script, so it reads any classic global safely; a leaf converted first would have classic consumers and need a bridge. A lib twin retires when its last classic consumer converts.

Shared leaves: a shared module is a leaf (it imports nothing and names no browser or Node global, `tests/unit/shared-modules.test.js`), served only through the explicit `SHARED_MODULES` allow-list in `lib/vendor-assets.js`, one route per file under the served /lib/ namespace, never by directory (a lib file not on the list is a 404). A page imports one with a relative specifier that starts with ../lib/ (quoted in the code). The second is `lib/time-words.js` (LIN-4472): the duration and relative-time words, which the server and the task page both import; the page's own copies were removed, not kept under a parity test. That resolves to the same file in the browser and in Node only because `public/` is served at the URL root and stays flat, with no nested .js files (`tests/unit/front-end-import-layout.test.js`). Do not move `public/` under a prefix or add a subdirectory.

One bridge, no new names: `public/cost-format-global.js` is the only module that writes a global for classic scripts. Its names, its one emitter and its classic readers are inventoried (`tests/unit/bridge-inventory.test.js`). A new name fails the check, and so does a registered reader that no longer reads, so the bridge only shrinks. A page that is a module imports the formatter directly and reads no bridge.

A bridge reader reads the global only from a handler or callback that runs after DOMContentLoaded, never while its script executes: Chart.js calls scale tick callbacks synchronously. Its witness loads the reader first and installs the global after it (`loadCostFormat`, `tests/fixtures/browser-cost-format.js`), which is the order a page has. The inventory reads each witness's calls and fails a witness whose first `loadCostFormat(` comes before it loads the reader.

A `{ module }` entry's place in a renderer's script list means nothing: a module runs after every classic script, wherever it is listed. A bridge reader is safe because of when it reads the global, not where the shim sits.

A converted page is tested by plain `import` over the fake DOM (`tests/unit/helpers/import-world.js`), not by `loadWorld`. Each import is a fresh module instance, and the world puts every global back when it is restored. The classic-loader census (`tests/unit/classic-loader-census.test.js`) is a ratchet on the suites that still load classic scripts: it may only fall. `importWorld` installs only what it is given, unlike `loadWorld`: no stub `fetch`, `setInterval` or clipboard, and real timers unless `timers` is passed, so a page's init would reach the network or leave a poll running. Test pure exports by a static import; drive an init through one shared world with inert defaults (`tests/unit/helpers/task-page-world.js`, LIN-4472), made before the import so the page's DOMContentLoaded listener lands on the fake document. A suite that runs a classic file through `runClassic` counts, except `public/chart-helpers.js` and `public/close-out.js`, the two IIFE siblings a module page may read.

A page module runs while `document.readyState` is already `'interactive'`, before DOMContentLoaded, so a module page that starts on DOMContentLoaded registers that listener unconditionally: its old `readyState === 'loading'` branch is false under a module and would start the page early. A top-level early return becomes `var mounted = ...` with the statements after it in `if (mounted) { }`: `var` stays module-scoped, and function declarations stay top-level and hoisted, as they were in the IIFE. (LIN-4463 piece 3, flight-companion.js.)

A module's exports are its test seams, and a namespace is read-only. A classic getter/setter pair on the export object becomes a named function (`getOpenLoopIds`/`setOpenLoopIds` in `public/observation.js`); a `let` read through the namespace is live. Keep each export's name from the old seam where it can stay a function (`lastRulingsRef`); an accessor named after its own state gains a verb (`openLoopIds` → `getOpenLoopIds`), so a suite changes how it loads and not what it asserts. A suite reaches module state through the seam, never by a script-scope probe. (LIN-4463 piece 4.)

`public/observation.js`: it is a module but still reads `public/common.js` globals bare (`escapeHtml`, `relativeTime`, `window.api`, `taskPageHref`/`sourceQuery`, `ReplyDelivery`, `ScanSection`), and each of its module suites (`tests/unit/observation-module.test.js`, `tests/unit/task-page-link-client-surfaces.test.js`, `tests/unit/observation-ruling-delivery.test.js`) rebuilds that contract by hand, differently: one stubs `escapeHtml` and `relativeTime`, one passes the real lib leaves, and the ruling-delivery suite runs `public/common.js` into the process global with `vm.runInThisContext` and an `importWorld({})` baseline it never restores (that keeps it in the classic-loader census). `public/flight-companion.js`: whether the page has its core mounts (`thread`, `questionInput`, `sendBtn`) is one decision spread over eight `if (mounted) { }` blocks (the first declares the turn state; the rest wire listeners and restore the stored session). Keep the missing-mount behaviour. Larger than a fix for a 2,200-line file; do it with the next change to this file. (LIN-4463 piece 3 blind read.)
